content: Given several PRs made by different persons, how is it possible to create a branch that merges all of them and start from there? I tried something such as creating a branch from one of those (gotten via gh pr checkout <some number>) and then tried gh pr merge <some other number> but that didn't work. I got a message suggesting adding --auto, but finally concluding that I am not authorized to merge.

What I usually do in this situation is pull all the branches onto my machine, check out the new branch I want to put them all in, and then git merge <name_of_branch> for each branch I want to merge into it.
I also do something similar to what Kevin does, but I wonder if there are some steps that are only available to maintainers, due to working from forks that are not your own.
You should always be able to fetch branches from other (public) forks and you can always create branches in your own fork. So there should be no permission issue.

I usually do it on web pages, create temporary branches on my own fork for PR from branch on other public fork. Only need to be more careful if there is merge conflict, this might really need some permission if you don't have a branch without conflict?
Merge within own fork seems being more friendly.
Sorry to mention that I once want to merge directly then broke a branch on Christian's fork ):

I think it makes a difference whether you use gh or git here.

Haven't verified but I believe gh pr merge might indeed write onto the branch of the other person's fork, which is something only reviewers+ are authorised to do. (there's a setting when creating a PR saying something like "allow reviewers to push [to the branch]" somewhere.)

But you should be able to use git checkout and git merge where you simply set the "remote" to point to the other person's fork and you work completeely inside your own fork.
Another thing I sometimes find useful is that you can check out specific files from a branch, e.g. git checkout master -- path/to/file. This can also be done for any remote.
